The proposal addresses all four Excellence aspects with a clearly integrated four-pillar structure, quantified supervisor credentials, and an unusually concrete triple-i training calendar, which justify a 'Very Good' rating. However, the complete absence of literature citations to substantiate 'beyond SOTA' claims, the templated repetition across the nine DC descriptions, and the predominance of process-based KPIs over scientific-depth metrics represent recurring, non-trivial shortcomings that keep the score below Excellent.

The proposal presents an ambitious, well-integrated four-pillar research programme with nine coherent DC projects and a genuinely novel regulatory-by-design causal-AI methodology, and pairs this with a detailed triple-i training calendar and a procedurally rich supervision structure (ITP/PCDP/Supervisory Board). However, KPIs are frequently process- rather than outcome-oriented, some methodological and open-science commitments remain generic, one supervisor profile is thinly evidenced, and the joint-supervision equivalence claim for a non-industrial/joint doctorate is asserted rather than demonstrated, keeping the proposal just short of the highest band despite its clear strengths.

The proposal addresses all four aspects comprehensively and coherently, with genuine structural strengths such as regulatory-integration-by-design and a well-articulated four-pillar framework linking all sections, meriting a 'very good' rating. However, recurring shortcomings — generic SOTA framing without citation-level specificity, templated and shallow DC-level technical detail, and anonymised supervisor profiles lacking concrete co-supervision evidence — keep it short of 'excellent', landing the score at 4.1.

The proposal presents an ambitious, well-structured four-pillar causal-AI programme with detailed DC descriptions, a coherent interdisciplinary methodology, a concrete triple-i training architecture, and senior, experienced supervisors with multi-layered governance (Sections 1.1-1.4), which together address all four aspects substantively. However, decisive weaknesses include largely rhetorical 'beyond SOTA' claims lacking named benchmarks or citations, under-specified causal-methodological choices, arbitrary/unvalidated KPI thresholds, and a self-serving claim of joint-supervision-equivalent quality despite not being a mandatory joint-supervision scheme. These shortcomings are real but do not undermine the overall coherence and ambition, placing the criterion solidly in the Very Good range with a number of shortcomings rather than Excellent.
